title: Kickstart engagement: StreamlineAI pilot acceptance matrix
summary: Practical kickoff and acceptance plan for a 6-week pilot with StreamlineAI (retail merchandising assistant). Focused on measurable throughput and quality SLAs, data-exchange guardrails, and clear go/no-go thresholds for moving to Dedicated capacity.
body:
Purpose:
This doc codifies the engagement plan, scope boundaries, and the acceptance matrix for StreamlineAI’s pilot of Redwood Inference. Goal is to validate: (1) latency and throughput under representative production traffic, (2) response quality for merchandising prompts, and (3) integration/pipeline stability for downstream systems.

Audience:
- StreamlineAI product and infra leads
- Redwood Solutions Engineering (owner: Priya Desai)
- Platform SRE and Security reviewers

High-level timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): data contracts, test harness, credentials, baseline metrics
- Week 1 (onboarding): environment setup in Redwood Hosted API + test model selection + warmup runs
- Week 2–3 (stress + quality cycles): synthetic load ramp + labeled prompt evals + instrumentation
- Week 4 (integration): end-to-end runs with StreamlineAI staging pipeline, error handling tests
- Week 5 (acceptance window): run acceptance matrices, collect metrics for SLA decision
- Week 6 (wrap/retrospect): business review, runbook handover, contract/next-step recommendation

Scope (what we will do):
- Host inference for two model variants: base-13B quantized and low-cost 7B variant for fallback.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latencies for token streaming and non-streaming flows across 3 sequence-length buckets (short: <128, medium: 128–512, long: 512+).
- Run an evaluation set of 500 labeled merchandising prompts with human judgments on: factuality, relevance, and actionability.
- Exercise automatic fallback routing and cold-start behavior under simulated capacity constraints.
- Provide temporary dashboard access and a short runbook for on-call steps.

Out of scope:
- Model training or fine-tuning within the engagement (we will use client-provided prompt templates and public model weights or Redwood-verified variants).
- Long-term data retention policy changes (these are handled by StreamlineAI infra).

Roles & contacts:
- Redwood SE lead: Priya Desai (pri@redwood.ai) — overall engagement owner
- StreamlineAI product lead: Jordan Patel — acceptance signoff
- Redwood SRE contact: Marcos Rivera — infra/runbook
- Data security reviewer: Tara O'Neill — data handling and KMS checks

Acceptance matrix (go/no-go criteria) — must meet all to be "Accepted":
1) Latency SLOs (measured across representative traffic):
   - Short sequence p95 < 120ms; medium p95 < 240ms; long p95 < 700ms.
   - p99 must not exceed 2x p95 for any bucket during the acceptance window.
2) Throughput & error budget:
   - Sustained throughput of 250 reqs/min for the baseline model with error rate < 0.5% (5xx and timeouts).
   - When autoscaling simulated load to 500 reqs/min, system maintains <2% error and exhibits graceful degradation (fallback to 7B variant) rather than hard failures.
3) Quality gates (human-evaluated):
   - On 500-prompt eval set, average score >= 3.5/5 for relevance and >= 3.2/5 for actionability.
   - No category of prompts (price updates, inventory-synced recommendations) shows systematic hallucination patterns in >10% of cases.
4) Integration & contract tests:
   - End-to-end pipeline completes within 90th percentile of expected time window for 95% of test cases.
   - Signed data contract + agreed masking/PII handling checklist by StreamlineAI infra.
5) Observability & runbook:
   - Dashboard exposes token-level cost, per-route latency, and error traces.
   - On-call runbook with 3 escalation steps, tested once during integration week.

Minimum success (if some acceptance items fail):
- If latency SLOs miss but quality gates pass, recommend acceptance with plan for Dedicated capacity uplift plus a 30-day performance SLA commitment.
- If quality gates fail, engagement is "remediation required" — propose a 3-week quality remediation sprint (prompt engineering, sampling instrumentation, targeted model variant adjustments).

Data & security notes:
- Use temporary staging API keys scoped to pilot; no long-term secrets stored in client code.
- All payloads with customer PII must be masked before being sent to Redwood (see masking checklist below).
- Optional: enable token-level logging with PII redaction for debug sessions only after signoff from Tara.

Instrumentation (what we will measure):
- Per-request: model variant, sequence length, tokens in/out, latency phases (queue, compute, stream), error codes
- Aggregates: p50/p95/p99 latencies per bucket, token throughput per GPU, cost per 1K tokens
- Quality: per-prompt scores and a small set of heuristic checks (entity hallucination detector, repetition rate)

Workshop agenda (onboarding + first evaluation, 2.5 hours):
- 00:00–00:15 Welcome, objectives, success criteria overview (Priya)
- 00:15–00:35 Environment walk-through: keys, dashboard, test harness (Marcos)
- 00:35–01:00 Prompting workshop: common templates, failure modes, evaluation rubric (StreamlineAI + Priya)
- 01:00–01:45 Live run: 50 representative prompts, real-time scoring and triage (all)
- 01:45–02:15 Instrumentation deep-dive: logs, dashboards, autoscaling knobs (Marcos + SRE)
- 02:15–02:30 Next steps, action items, and responsibilities (Priya)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: bursty traffic causes long p99 spikes. Mitigation: enforce pre-warm policy, synthetic ramp testing, and temporary throttling with backlog alerts.
- Risk: integration failures due to payload schema drift. Mitigation: add contract tests to PR gating and a schema validation step in staging.
- Risk: quality regressions after model variant change. Mitigation: pin version during acceptance window; use A/B rollouts for any changes.

Deliverables at close of pilot:
- Acceptance report (quantitative metrics + human eval summary)
- Small runbook and dashboard access for StreamlineAI operators
- Recommendation memo: move to Dedicated / Hosted long-term / Remediation plan

Immediate next steps (after kickoff meeting):
1) Agree and sign the one-page pilot charter (owner: StreamlineAI product lead)
2) Exchange staging credentials and data contract (owner: StreamlineAI infra)
3) Redwood to provision test environment and import eval prompts (owner: Priya)
4) Schedule the onboarding workshop (owner: Priya + Marcos)

Notes to SEs (working reminders):
- Keep the eval set balanced across content types: price changes, localized promotions, inventory-driven messages, cross-sell suggestions.
- Capture at least 30 human-judged failure examples to feed back into prompt guidelines.
- Track cost delta between base/7B variants to quantify unit economics for Dedicated sizing.

Appendix — masking checklist (short):
- Remove or hash raw customer email addresses and phone numbers
- Zero-out payment tokens and account numbers
- For any merchant PII (supplier IDs), replace with pseudonymous IDs and keep mapping locally with client only

End of doc.

Document history: initial draft by Priya Desai (2025-11-20). Reviewed by Marcos and Alex on 2025-11-28. Updated acceptance thresholds after joint call with StreamlineAI on 2025-12-02.
